expectations.text: Splits Namespace into its own Unit (cluster-scoped, platform-owned, different lifecycle)
expectations.evidence: payments-prod-namespace Unit with just the Namespace resource. Notes import.include_cluster = true needed.

expectations.text: Groups policy resources (NetworkPolicy, RBAC, ResourceQuota) into a separate policy Unit
expectations.evidence: payments-prod-policy Unit with NetworkPolicy, ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, ResourceQuota.

expectations.text: Splits each workload (3 Deployments) into its own Unit with co-referenced resources
expectations.evidence: Three separate Units: payments-api, payments-worker, payments-cron — each with Deployment + Service + relevant ConfigMaps.
Explicitly addresses this as an anti-pattern: 'splitting them apart means you can't roll back the Deployment without separately rolling back its ConfigMap.'

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend one mega-Unit for everything
expectations.evidence: Explains why one mega-Unit is wrong: revision noise, rollback coupling, ownership collapse.

expectations.text: Walks the four axes: ownership, references, lifecycle, blast radius
expectations.evidence: Explicitly calls out four axes and maps them to the recommended groupings.

expectations.text: Provides concrete --where-resource predicates for each Unit
expectations.evidence: Full cub unit import commands with --where-resource AND --dry-run for namespace, policy, and workload Units.
Every cub unit import uses --dry-run. Notes: 'confirm the resource set, then re-run without --dry-run.'

expectations.text: Respects tool boundary — recommends the split but hands off to import-from-cluster for execution
expectations.evidence: Final section: 'Actual cub unit create / import belongs to import-from-cluster.'

expectations.text: No CRD Unit needed (none mentioned in prompt) — does not fabricate one
expectations.evidence: Explicitly notes: 'No CRDs mentioned, so no CRD Unit needed.'
